source.title: Disentangling pleasure from incentive salience and learning signals in brain reward circuitry.
source.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences

confidence_rationale: Direct neural dissociation: dopamine stimulation in nucleus accumbens enhanced ONLY the motivation/incentive-salience component and did NOT alter hedonic impact or learned-prediction signals; the incentive-salience signal to the reward-proximal cue was separable from the learned prediction value of the distal cue. This is strong, mechanistically specific support for MECH-347's 'cue-pull with no revaluation' (incentive salience independent of value-update). Docked for rat ventral-pallidum/accumbens electrophysiology vs REE latent nudge.
failure_signatures: Incentive salience enhancement required pharmacological dopamine stimulation; a purely cue-driven nudge without a gain/state signal may not reproduce the effect magnitude.

Incentive salience tracked the reward-PROXIMAL cue, not the distal predictive cue, so cue_pull strength should scale with proximity (consistent with REE's cue_recall_min_proximity) rather than mere predictive association.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Wanting (incentive salience), liking, and learned prediction are represented by separable signals in accumbens-pallidum circuitry; dopamine stimulation amplified only the motivation component without changing learned-prediction signals.
mapping.ree_translation: Supports MECH-347's design that cue_pull nudges the goal (wanting) WITHOUT triggering a benefit gate or revaluation: the biology shows the wanting signal can be amplified while learned-prediction (value) signals are untouched, exactly the dissociation cue_pull assumes.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The dissociation was produced by intra-accumbens drug microinjection; REE has no pharmacological analog and instantiates the nudge as a fixed-gain directional shift. The paper shows wanting CAN be dissociated from value, not that an ungated nudge is the normal driver.
mapping.source_context: Rats, Pavlovian cue sequence for sucrose; ventral pallidum single-unit firing with intra-accumbens opioid vs dopamine microinjection.

confidence_components.notes: Strong mechanistic dissociation directly matching the no-revaluation premise; transfer risk from rodent pharmacology to a latent nudge.
